## How Much Funding Has Discovered Materials Raised?  
Discovered Materials has successfully raised funds through 1 rounds, with the latest being a Seed led by Lightspeed India Partners. With a total of $9M raised, the company continues to expand its operations.  
Lead Investors  
Lightspeed India Partners  
Valuation at Round  
Not publicly disclosed  
Motivation Behind the Round  
Lightspeed India Partners led Discovered Materials' $9 million seed round, with Y Combinator and Peak XV Partners also participating alongside angel investors Paul Graham, Gokul Rajaram, and Thariq Shihipar of Anthropic. Hemant Mohapatra, the Lightspeed partner who led the round, cited the founders' rare combination of deep materials science expertise and frontier AI engineering as the primary investment thesis. The round was announced alongside the release of Material Discovery Bench and hundreds of new AI-discovered materials, providing third-party validation of the research pipeline's output quality. Capital will be used to expand the team and laboratory operations and scale the company's AI research agent infrastructure.  
Total Amount Raised: $9M
## Key Investors  
Lightspeed India Partners  
Venture Capital  
Lightspeed India Partners led Discovered Materials' seed round. Partner Hemant Mohapatra, who led the investment, described the problem as a search challenge where a material is only useful if all of its required properties converge simultaneously. Lightspeed's thesis for the investment centers on the urgency of the heat dissipation problem in AI chip packaging and the founders' combination of Stanford materials science depth and frontier AI engineering capability.  
Y Combinator  
Accelerator  
Y Combinator backed Discovered Materials through its Spring 2026 batch before the seed round. The company is one of several YC-backed startups working on AI-accelerated materials discovery, but is differentiated by its focus on the semiconductor thermal problem and its team's direct experience placing materials into chipmaker roadmaps.  
Peak XV Partners  
Venture Capital  
Peak XV Partners, formerly Sequoia India, participated in Discovered Materials' seed round. The firm has backed a number of deep tech and AI companies with Indian founders and has an active interest in semiconductor and AI infrastructure investments.
